assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only legend-of-the-galactic-heroes:yang-wen-li@original-novels#dedicated-character-and-philosophy-monograph, the canonical 03_YANG_WENLI_CHARACTER_AND_PHILOSOPHY.md (v1.0, 2026-08-10) at basis_commit, read in full. Its front matter names primary sources M01-M10, G02, G03 and G04 of Tanaka Yoshiki's Japanese prose. Its locators are volume-chapter (for example M03-C09, G04-C08), with a few quoted Japanese passages. It defers Yang's full relational treatment to Documents 04 and 06, case-by-case deception ethics to Document 10 and the verified Japanese term index to Document 15. Those documents, the Document 14 evidence ledger and the other LOGH syntheses are not curated on this subject and are not used. Anime, manga and other adaptations are outside the subject. The evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The monograph's seven developmental phases: merchant's son and reluctant cadet (M01-C02), unwanted hero of El Facil (G04-C01-02), miracle commander (M01), democratic military guardian through the coup and inquiry (M02-M03), near-sovereign who refuses sovereignty at Vermilion and in retirement (M05-M06), republican remnant leader (M06-M08), and death on June 1, Space Year 800 (M08-C05). Posthumous Yang (M08-M10) is memory and political use, not Yang's own conduct; the monograph says it gives no direct access to his will. The monograph warns against projecting later doctrine back onto the child. Claims apply to the living Yang at a named phase.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph gives a coherent interpretive model that it tests against counterreadings. Its core is a historian forced into command who does not infer jurisdiction from accuracy (I, VI.5). It adds inward skepticism shading into self-erasure (VI.2, M08-C03), spiral thought as both strength and delay (V.4, G04-C06), humor as anti-idolatry (VI.3), and reluctance with three functions: aversion, principled refusal and avoidance (II). It also names a failure mode, principled under-assertion (XIX.6, XXIII). C, not D: these are integrated, phase-aware and tied to located decisions. Not B: the model is a literary-philosophical synthesis with chapter-level locators and few quoted passages. It states no conditional behavior rules beyond major political-military decisions and has no validation artifact.

Section II's phase table ties each identity, stable traits and developmental change to volumes, and Section IX reads the campaigns as a sequence in which each adds a different political burden: Astarte, Iserlohn, Amritsar, coup suppression, Geiersburg, Vermilion and the corridor. Section XVI.2 tracks how Reinhard forces his theory to mature from defending Alliance procedure to preserving one republican seed. The monograph cautions against backward projection (II) and separates living from posthumous Yang (XXII.9). Not B: phase boundaries are volume-range summaries with little scene-level state evidence inside each phase.

Section XVIII characterizes the voice. He uses 私, not Reinhard's 予, and hedges with と思う, かな and どうだろう-type uncertainty. He deflates with irony, keeps formal language toward superiors that can carry quiet resistance, and pairs a soft voice with hard limits; irony thins under stress. Quoted Yang wording is limited to a few principle statements (M03-C06, M03-C09) and one interior reflection (M01-C02). The verified term index is deferred to Document 15, which is not curated here. D, not C: patterns are named but barely exemplified, so register can be described but not reproduced. Not E: the patterns are explicit and contrasted with another speaker.

Section XVII treats tea, books, the pension wish and domestic disorder as character evidence. He depends on Julian for meals and tea and on Frederica for organization (XIV.1, XIII.2), and his slouch and dislike of ceremony puncture the hero image (IV.4). These are thematic, not scene-located: the section gives no chapter locators, and no ordinary task is reconstructed step by step. Not E: the habits are stable, cross-phase and explicitly interpreted.

Differentiated stances are summarized for several counterparts. With Julian he teaches through conversation, irony and visible self-limits while depending on him at home (XIV). Frederica supplies procedure and emotional directness where he deflects (XIII). Toward Reinhard he admires without hatred or capitulation (XVI). With civilian superiors his formal language carries quiet resistance and bounded obedience (X.3, XVIII.4). He rejects Schönkopf's repeated dictatorship invitations (VII.2, XI). Subordinates disagree and tease within a plural staff (XV.2). D, not C: the monograph explicitly defers the full relational treatment to Documents 04 and 06, and most stances are summarized without located exchanges.

The monograph locates narrated interior access. His reflection that a person does not become free merely by being a person (M01-C02) is quoted. The narrator's statement that his mind was always a historian's, never a judicial officer's (G04-C08), is quoted. It also locates his questioning at Econia (G04-C06), his doubt in M08-C03 whether his defeat or absence might give followers a richer future, and his wondering who would care for him without the heroic aura (G04-C02). C, not D: interior states are located across phases and distinguished from narrator and legend. Not B: only a handful of passages are quoted, and inner states during most decisions are inferred from conduct.

Military and political conflict behavior is the monograph's fullest operational content. The command profile table (VIII.7) covers preferred level, information style, risk tolerance, delegation, casualty concern, termination logic, strongest opponent type and failure mode. Section VIII covers preservation, positional control (宙域管制, M07), logistics, deception and strategic patience. Section IX.1 gives a recurring five-step Astarte pattern. C, not D: this is a structured, located account of how he fights and when he stops. Not B: it is campaign-level, not decision-by-decision, and gives little on interpersonal conflict outside command.

Ethical reasoning is reconstructed with located decisions and both sides argued. Civilian supremacy against the coup (M02-C03-06) and the inquiry (M03-C05-06) are covered, with quoted principles at M03-C06 and M03-C09. Vermilion (M05-C07-09) gets explicit defense, critique and assessment (IX.6, XIX.1). The monograph lists what he will and will not claim (XI.6) and covers covert force after his arrest (XIX.2) and the greenhouse modesty of M08-C03 (VII.6). C, not D: the reasoning is principled, located and tested against counter-cases (XI.5). Not B, though B was the closest call: the account covers major political-military legitimacy decisions only, defers case-by-case deception ethics to an uncurated document, and reconstructs reasons at chapter level, not from passage-level deliberation.

Humor is treated as a stable trait with a political function (VI.3, IV.4, XVIII.3): jokes about pensions, tea, laziness and bureaucratic absurdity. It is inherited in rhythm from his father (III.1). The monograph also notes that irony can evade emotional directness. No joke is quoted or located by chapter, so the trait can be described but not reproduced.

One dedicated monograph covers his whole arc across M01-M10 and three gaiden volumes, with explicit evidence cautions (XXII). Depth is uneven. Locators are chapter-level. Relational, deception-ethics and Japanese-voice treatment are deferred to uncurated documents, and the row's coverage note (ten main novels and five gaiden) is broader than the monograph's own primary-source list (M01-M10, G02-G04). Not B: one synthesis document carries every claim.

Affirmative limits are stated and located. He is not a pacifist and kills at massive scale (VIII, XXII.6). He uses deception and benefits from coercion he did not initiate (VIII.4, XIX.2). His household competence is poor (XVII.3). He prefers retirement to institution-building (XII.2, XVII.5) and under-asserts legitimate authority (XIX.6). His philosophy is not the narrator's doctrine (XXII.1), and Vermilion remains contested (XXII.3). C, not D: limits are explicit, cross-phase and argued. Not B: they are interpretive conclusions at chapter level.

The phase table, the campaign sequence and the death date (June 1, SE 800, M08-C05) anchor claims to volumes and events. The monograph separates the child's intuitions from later doctrine and the living from the posthumous Yang. Not B: positions within a phase are not dated, and most claims cite volume ranges.

scenario_readiness.note: Named voice patterns without a quoted dialogue corpus cannot support source-faithful lines. Generated speech would be a fluent imitation of the described hedges and irony, not attested voice. The verified term index is uncurated. This bounds the evidence set, not Yang's speech.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: The living Yang at one named developmental phase between M01 and M08-C05; posthumous memory excluded.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Julian, Frederica, Reinhard, civilian superiors, Schönkopf or the Yang Fleet staff as the monograph summarizes them; the refusal applies equally to any other counterpart.
setting_constraints: Counterfactual careers, the denied Reinhard meeting, crossovers or materially novel settings
Behavioral or dialogue simulation rather than bounded canon description

scenario_readiness.note: The monograph itself marks counterfactual political careers as speculative (XXII.7) and the Reinhard meeting as unknowable (XVI.4, XXII.8). Its model is built from major political-military decisions inside the novels and gives no basis for materially novel contexts.
Tea, books, pension jokes and domestic dependence are stable but unlocated habits. They answer canon questions about his ordinary life but support no simulation of ordinary social scenes.

conditions: Only questions of civil-military legitimacy, seizure or refusal of sovereignty, obedience to civilian authority, and bounded war aims structurally analogous to the coup, inquiry, Vermilion, retirement or republican-remnant decisions.
The living Yang at a named phase, with the phase's stated doctrine; later doctrine is not projected backward.
Output is a reasoned position summary attributed as interpretation, not dialogue; for contested cases such as Vermilion, both the defense and the indictment are kept.
Case-by-case deception ethics and the conduct of his followers' covert force are not supplied.
scenario_readiness.note: The monograph reconstructs his reasoning on civil-military legitimacy with located decisions, quoted principles and both sides argued. That supports bounded summaries of how he would weigh analogous questions, not open moral simulation.
Frederica's marriage and partnership are summarized (XIII) with relational detail deferred to an uncurated document. No exchange is reconstructed, so a romance scenario would be invention.

conditions: Only operational-strategic judgments analogous to Astarte, Iserlohn, Amritsar, coup suppression, Geiersburg, Vermilion or the corridor campaign: preservation, positional control, logistics, deception and termination.
Summary-level reasoning attributed as interpretation; no invented tactical specifics, orders or staff dialogue.
Strategic choices stay subordinate to his stated political limits (civilian supremacy, bounded objectives).
No civil administration, party politics or peacetime statecraft; the monograph treats such careers as speculative.
scenario_readiness.note: The command profile and campaign logic support bounded description of his operational-strategic reasoning in situations like the located campaigns.

known_limits.statement: Yang's democratic philosophy is articulated strongly but is not the narrator's unquestioned doctrine; the novels expose its costs.
Yang is not a pacifist. His operations kill at massive scale, use deception, and seek Reinhard's death or capture at Vermilion; his ethic is anti-waste, not nonviolence.
Obedience at Vermilion is morally contested. Calling it simply correct erases casualties and collapse; calling it betrayal erases the civil-supremacy principle.
Counterfactual careers (elected reformer, benevolent dictator, peacetime statesman) are speculative, and the outcome of the denied meeting with Reinhard is unknowable.
Posthumous rhetoric about Yang is evidence of memory and political use, not direct access to his will.
His reluctance has multiple causes (personal laziness, trauma, vocation, humility, constitutional principle) that should not be collapsed into one motive.
The monograph defers relational treatment (Documents 04, 06), deception ethics (Document 10) and the Japanese term index (Document 15); none is curated on this subject.
Most claims are located only at volume-chapter level, with few quoted passages and no fidelity or validation artifact.
The evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
